body:
• Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. posted record August revenue of NT$514.8 billion ($16.3 billion), up 53.3% from a year earlier — its fourth consecutive monthly record and the first month above NT$500 billion.
  • The chipmaker's 5/4nm and 3nm capacity is fully booked on AI server GPU and XPU demand, while Apple's iPhone buildup and first 2nm revenue added to the surge, according to TrendForce.
  • Investors barely reacted: TSMC's U.S.-listed shares slipped 2.2% on Thursday, and shares of AMD, Broadcom and Nvidia fell too — a sign the AI boom's numbers are already priced in.
  • One looming worry for customers: Reuters reported in July that TSMC plans price increases of up to 10% starting next year.

The numbers

TSMC said August sales rose 10.1% from July to NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3% year on year, according to its monthly filing cited by TrendForce. Revenue for the first eight months of 2026 totaled NT$3.39 trillion, up 39.3% from the same period last year. The company guided third-quarter revenue of US$44.6 billion to US$45.8 billion, up about 12% sequentially at the midpoint, Taiwan's Central News Agency reported.

Chairman C.C. Wei has told investors he expects U.S.-dollar revenue to grow more than 40% in 2026, which would make it one of the strongest years in the company's history.

What is driving it

Two forces are doing the heavy lifting. The first is artificial intelligence: TrendForce says strong demand for AI server GPUs and XPUs has kept TSMC's 5/4nm and 3nm capacity fully booked, pushing up both wafer shipments and average selling prices. The second is smartphones: Apple's rollout of the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max — all powered by A20 Pro chips built on TSMC's 2nm process — triggered an inventory buildup that supported August sales, and 2nm contributed revenue for the first time.

The foundry market numbers show how dominant TSMC has become. TrendForce estimates its share of second-quarter foundry revenue climbed to 72.5%, up from 72.3% in the first quarter, far ahead of Samsung at 5.9% and SMIC at 5.4%. Global foundry revenue jumped to $53.5 billion in the second quarter, the firm said.

A market that shrugs at records

The striking part of Thursday's session was how little the record mattered to the stock. TSMC's American depositary receipts fell 2.2% in early trading. Investors, as Barron's put it, "have gotten used to eye-popping sales numbers from TSMC as the AI boom drives up demand for its chips." Shares of AMD, Broadcom and Nvidia — all TSMC customers — slid on Thursday as well, suggesting the monthly figure failed to revive a broader AI trade that has, in Barron's words, "run out of gas lately."

Macro headwinds added to the gloom: Brent crude futures climbed to just below $105 a barrel and bond yields crept higher, pressuring tech stocks across the board.

There is also a pricing cloud on the horizon. TSMC plans to raise prices by up to 10% from next year, Reuters reported in July, citing two sources familiar with the matter. TSMC did not respond to Barron's request for comment. For chip designers that depend on the foundry, that pricing power — built on a dominant market share — is a double-edged sword: it guarantees TSMC's margins while raising costs for everyone else in the supply chain.

Portfolio implications

For investors, TSMC remains the single most important node in the AI supply chain. It makes the chips inside Nvidia's accelerators — the standard for training AI models — and inside Apple's iPhones, which makes its monthly revenue reports a widely watched barometer of AI demand. Record sales confirm demand is still running hot; the muted stock reaction suggests the market now takes that for granted and is asking what comes next: pricing power, margins, and whether the foundry's planned price increases signal confidence or the top of the cycle.

What is next

September's sales figures, due next month, will show whether TSMC can extend its record streak to five months and hit the top end of its third-quarter guidance. Investors will also watch for any confirmation of the reported price increases — a move that would widen margins but test customer relationships at the height of an AI capital-spending cycle. With 2nm production now contributing revenue, the ramp of Apple's new iPhone lineup through the holiday quarter will be the next demand signal to watch.
diaspora_angle: TSMC anchors most semiconductor and emerging-market index funds held by global investors, so its guidance and pricing power shape portfolios well beyond Taiwan.
headline: TSMC Posts Record August Revenue as AI Boom Keeps Foundries Fully Booked
subheadline: Taiwan Semiconductor posted NT$514.8 billion in August sales — up 53% from a year ago — but investors barely blinked, with the stock slipping as the AI trade shows signs of fatigue.
